subject: ela
intro: Eleventh graders analyze multiple interpretations of a story, drama, or poem (for example, recorded or live productions of a play, or recorded novels or poetry), evaluating how each version interprets the source text. Different productions make different choices and emphasize different aspects of the same work.

items.prompt:
Two staged productions of the same play portray the lead as a hero in one and a villain in the other.

What accounts for the difference?

steps: Each production interprets the ambiguous character differently through direction and acting.
So the difference reflects each production's interpretation of the source.
solution.answer: Each production interprets the same character differently through its choices.

items.prompt:
One film of a novel sets it in the original era; another updates it to the present.

How does each INTERPRET the source?

steps: The faithful setting stresses historical context; the modern setting stresses the story's timeless relevance.
So each interprets the source to emphasize a different aspect.
solution.answer: One stresses historical context; the other stresses timeless relevance.

items.prompt: Why evaluate MULTIPLE interpretations of one work?

steps: Comparing interpretations reveals the work's range of possible meanings.
So it deepens understanding of the source's possibilities.
solution.answer: It reveals the range of meanings the source can support.

items.prompt: A production's take on a text is its ____.
The original text is the ____ text.
